answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation to a scarce, verifiable resource: each agent must lock a deposit and build a history of useful work before it can transact at scale. A newcomer arrives like a comet, bright and fast but unproven, while a trusted agent stands on a knoll of accumulated attestations that peers can check. Splitting one deposit across many fake identities leaves each stranded on a flat mesa of low trust, unable to reach the tier where valuable work lives. Reputation earned slowly is the cost that makes mass sybils uneconomic.
